messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "The weather’s been so unpredictable lately—seems like everyone’s quietly making plans for the fall, even the ones who used to just wait and see. Still, everything feels… arranged, like the gears are turning but no one’s saying what for."
Sender 2: "Just had a quiet dinner with the usual group — everything’s running normally, even the bus route got extended last week. Funny how no one’s talking about politics at all, not even at a three-day wedding. Feels like the air’s changed, but I can’t tell if we’re calm or just holding our breath."
Sender 3: "Just heard the new bakery on 5th finally opened — apparently, they’ve been waiting on permits for months. Guess the system still works, even if nothing else does. Be careful what you share these days — some things are better left unsaid."
Sender 4: "The market ladies are naming names now—no more whispers. Feels like the walls are thinning, and everyone’s starting to plan ahead, not just survive. Keep your eyes open, but your mouths closed."
Sender 5: "I’ve been thinking — something’s shifting under the surface. The quiet now feels heavier than the noise ever did. Let’s keep our heads down, but stay sharp."
Sender 6: "Just got back from the market — the usual crowd, but something’s off. The baker said the bread’s been the same for weeks, but the air feels different, like everyone’s holding their breath. Might be nothing, but I’ve been thinking… maybe we should keep our phones charged, just in case."
Sender 7: "The streets feel different—people are talking, not just about the weather or the markets, but about what comes next. I’ve heard whispers everywhere, and the silence from the usual sources is louder than any announcement. Let’s stay sharp, keep quiet, and watch the rhythm of the city."
Sender 8: "Just got back from the market — saw a few familiar faces, same routines, but there’s a quietness to it all, like everyone’s waiting for the next chapter to start. The shops are full, the streets busy, but I’ve been hearing whispers about people packing up, shifting plans, even the ones who seem most settled. Whatever’s coming, it’s not coming fast, but it might not be far. Keep your eyes open."
Sender 9: "The weather’s been strange lately—warm one day, freezing the next. My landlord asked about relatives abroad last week, just offhand, like he was checking the forecast. Be careful what you say, even to people you’ve known a long time."
Sender 10: "Just got word from someone in the district office—transfers are frozen, and the usual channels are all quiet. Whatever’s coming, it’s moving faster than we thought. Keep your ears open, but don’t speak unless you have to."

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 10 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 10.
